abstractTitle: Cancer Detection in Histopathological Images and an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Assisted Decision System
abstractText: Histopathological examination, accepted as the gold standard in cancer diagnosis, increases the need for artificial intelligence-assisted systems due to observer-dependent variability in manual assessment and increasing workload. This project aims to develop an explainable artificial intelligence system capable of analyzing multiple cancer types using five open datasets related to breast cancer, breast lymph node metastasis, lung cancer, and colon cancer. The models, trained with more than 530,000 histopathological images in total, were developed using an EfficientNet-based transfer learning approach and a standard preprocessing pipeline. The breast cancer model was specialized with a three-stage progressive transfer learning strategy, achieving 82% accuracy on the IDC dataset with patient-based separation, 96% in the second stage transferred to the BACH dataset, and 88% accuracy with 0.90 ROC-AUC on the final BreakHis model. In patient-based evaluations performed on the BreakHis dataset, the 200x magnification model stood out in screening scenarios with its high malignant sensitivity, while the model covering all magnification ratios offered more balanced classification performance. The breast cancer lymph node metastasis model achieved 95% accuracy. The lung and colon cancer models reached 100% accuracy, although the literature recommends validating the generalizability of this performance with different datasets. In order to make AI model decisions explainable (XAI), the Grad-CAM method was applied, and tissue regions influential in classification were visualized with heat maps. The system architecture was built on a modular structure in which an MVC-based web application and an AI microservice provided through a Flask-based REST API work separately, while image upload, classification, and explainability outputs are presented on a single platform. In this respect, the project presents scientific AI models with R&D value and a prototype AI assistant that can be used for clinical pre-assessment.
